issues.legal_issue: Concurrent findings of fact do not bar a second appeal when an established legal exception gives rise to a substantial question of law.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court both granted an injunction based on their conclusion that the disputed land was outside a protected forest area.
The High Court dismissed the second appeals essentially because both lower courts had reached the same conclusion.
The dispute raised questions about the land’s classification and compliance with applicable forest, revenue and mining laws.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was wrong to treat the concurrent findings as making the second appeals unassailable. A substantial question of law arises where a concurrent finding is shown to fall within a recognised exception, and the questions raised in these appeals required consideration on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, concurrent findings of fact are usually binding in a second appeal, but not where a finding was made de hors the pleadings, based on no evidence, based on a misreading of material documentary evidence, contrary to a provision of law, or is one that no judge acting judicially could reasonably have reached. Any such ground, if established on the pleadings and evidence, constitutes a substantial question of law. The Court relied on Rajeshwar Vishwanath Mamidwar v. Dashrath Narayan Chilwelkar, AIR 1943 Nagpur 117, paragraph 43.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_factual_findings and (finding_outside_pleadings or finding_based_on_no_evidence or finding_based_on_misreading_material_documents or finding_contrary_to_law or finding_unreasonable)

predicates.second_appeal: The challenged decision is being considered in a second appeal.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual finding.
predicates.finding_outside_pleadings: The challenged finding was made without being grounded in the parties’ pleadings.
predicates.finding_based_on_no_evidence: The challenged finding was made without supporting evidence.
predicates.finding_based_on_misreading_material_doc: The challenged finding rests on a misreading of material documentary evidence.
predicates.finding_contrary_to_law: The challenged finding conflicts with a provision of law.
predicates.finding_unreasonable: The challenged decision is one that no judge acting judicially could reasonably have reached.

issues.definition: When a second appeal challenges concurrent factual findings and at least one stated defect applies, a substantial question of law arises.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court must frame and decide substantial questions of law arising from the pleadings, evidence and applicable law rather than dismiss a second appeal merely because the lower courts made concurrent findings.
material_facts: The suit sought an injunction to prevent interference with mining operations on disputed land.
The parties disputed whether the land was protected forest land or revenue land and whether the relevant statutory requirements for the land and mining lease had been met.
The High Court dismissed the second appeals without examining the identified questions on their merits, relying essentially on the concurrent findings below.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have admitted the second appeals, framed the appropriate substantial questions of law and answered them on their merits. The Supreme Court set aside the dismissal and remanded the appeals for that purpose without expressing an opinion on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, requires a second appeal involving substantial questions of law to be considered on those questions. Questions about land classification, compliance with applicable forest, revenue and mining laws, the maintainability of the suit, and the basis for an injunction could not be avoided merely because the lower courts agreed. The Court directed the High Court to frame questions in light of the pleadings, evidence, lower-court findings and relevant laws.

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding before the High Court is a second appeal.
predicates.substantial_questions_arise_from_pleadin: The pleadings, evidence and applicable law raise substantial questions requiring determination.
predicates.high_court_dismissed_without_examining_t: The High Court dismissed the appeal without examining the substantial questions that arose.

issues.definition: When a second appeal raises substantial questions from the case materials and the High Court dismisses it without examining them, the appeal must be decided on framed substantial questions.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal does not abate on the death of a respondent when a legal representative is already on record, and remaining representatives may be brought on record after remand.
material_facts: The plaintiff died while the appeals were pending.
His wife was already on record in connected appeals or suits, and the related matters had been clubbed for disposal.
The Supreme Court remanded the pending appeals, allowing consequential steps to bring any remaining legal representatives on record.
issues.conclusion: The appeals had not abated. The parties could amend the cause title after remand to substitute the surviving wife and any other legal representatives before the second appeals were heard.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, in the circumstances, the presence of one legal representative on record meant the appeal did not abate; the connected proceedings and the opportunity to take consequential steps after remand also supported that conclusion. The judgment cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this ruling.

rule.if: appeal_pending and respondent_died_during_appeal and legal_representative_already_on_record and (connected_proceedings_grouped or remand_allows_remaining_representatives_to_be_added)

predicates.appeal_pending: An appeal is pending when a respondent dies.
predicates.respondent_died_during_appeal: A respondent dies while the appeal is pending.
predicates.legal_representative_already_on_record: At least one legal representative of the deceased respondent is already a party on the record.
predicates.connected_proceedings_grouped: The appeal is being dealt with together with connected proceedings involving the deceased respondent’s legal representative.
predicates.remand_allows_remaining_representatives_: The matter is remanded in circumstances that allow any remaining legal representatives to be added before further hearing.

issues.definition: When a respondent dies during a pending appeal, a legal representative is already on record, and the stated connection or remand condition applies, the appeal does not abate.
